_about.purpose: Measure chunk retrieval quality for DocumentChatSkill, separately from answer quality.
_about.match: 'any' = a hit if any expected source is selected. 'all' = every expected source must be selected (cross-boundary answers).

categories.direct: The answering chunk shares obvious wording with the question.
categories.vocab_overlap: A distractor chunk shares more surface words with the question than the chunk that actually answers it.
categories.cross_boundary: The answer needs two chunks; neither is sufficient alone.
categories.synonym: The question shares no content word with the answering chunk.
categories.dilution: The answering sentence sits inside a page covering several unrelated topics, so a whole-page embedding averages it with material that has nothing to do with the question.
categories.topical_sibling: Two or more pages are plausibly on-topic for the question, but only one carries the figure being asked for.

_about.trivial_note: These three fixtures have only 2 chunks each and the selector returns top-3 plus first/last anchors, so it returns the whole document for any query. Retrieval accuracy on them is 100% by construction and carries no signal. They are kept to prove the eval harness agrees with reality, and are reported separately.

_about.purpose: Measure retrieval and ATTRIBUTION when one question is asked across a whole corpus, not one document.
_about.why_separate: Scored apart from the single-document set so neither number contaminates the other. The single-document headline (33/33 retrieved, 28/33 ranked first) is quoted in the docs and must stay comparable across sessions, and cross-corpus retrieval fails for different reasons than in-document retrieval does.
_about.expected_sources: A source is a {doc, source} PAIR, not a bare page number. That is the whole point: page 3 of the operations review and page 3 of the staff manual are different sources, and the single-document code cannot tell them apart because it keys on the page label alone.

categories.one_of_many: The fact lives in exactly one document; the others are on-topic but silent on it.
categories.topical_sibling: Two documents are plausibly the right place to look, but only one carries the figure.
categories.cross_document: The answer needs a fact from each of two different documents. Neither answers alone.
categories.wrong_document: The highest-scoring passage is in a document that does NOT hold the answer, so a selector with fewer slots - or a reader trusting an unqualified page number - lands on the wrong document.

_about.corpus_note: All six fixtures are used, including the three trivial ones. They are not filler here: they are what makes page labels collide. Pages 1 and 2 exist in four of the six documents, so a citation of Page 1 names four different things.
_about.expected_answer_all: Every fragment must appear: the question asks two things and half an answer is wrong. Distinct from expected_answer_contains, which is a list of alternative phrasings of ONE fact and is satisfied by any of them.
_about.no_answer_cases: Questions the corpus does NOT answer. Scored on whether the model DECLINES, which nothing else here measures: every other case has an answer, so a model that simply always answers scores perfectly on them. Pass is `declined`, not `avoided the trap value`. A reply that says 'the manual gives 45 pence for a private vehicle but states no motorcycle rate' MENTIONS a trap value while declining correctly, and that is the right answer. `asserted_trap` is therefore reported as a diagnostic, not as the verdict. Needs --with-answers: declining is a property of generation, and there is nothing to score without a reply.

no_answer_categories.no_answer_anywhere: Nothing in any loaded document touches the subject.
no_answer_categories.answer_absent_document: The corpus covers the topic area, but the document holding this particular fact is not loaded. The realistic case: a user asks about something they have not uploaded.
no_answer_categories.near_miss: The retrieved context does NOT contain the answer but DOES contain a plausible substitute — the same measure for a different depot, tier, quarter or organisation. This is the md-10 shape and the hard one: the substitute is on-topic, so retrieval scores it highly and cannot flag it.

_about.no_answer_expects_decline: true = nothing in the corpus answers this, so the reply must decline. false = part of the question IS answerable, so declining outright would be wrong; the criterion is instead that the named trap value must not appear.

no_answer_cases.question: How many people does the company employ, and what is the standard annual leave entitlement?
no_answer_cases.note: md-10's exact question, scored on FABRICATION rather than on declining. Asked on its own, 'how many people does the company employ' retrieves review page 1 at slot 6 and is answered correctly as 1,840. Adding the leave half is what breaks it: three of the six slots go to leave, page 1 drops out, and a sheet named Headcount holding another company's departmental numbers is the closest thing left. So this is a SLOT BUDGET interaction with multi-part questions, not a retrieval-quality failure. Declining outright would be WRONG here — the leave half is genuinely answerable — so the criterion is that 96 must not appear. 96 is computed (51+21+15+9) and exists nowhere in any document, so any occurrence is fabrication, not a mention.

_about.purpose: Does mixing topics on a page cost the answering passage its rank?
_about.design: 3x3 factorial. Topic count 1 (control), 2, 6 crossed with the answering fact leading the page, sitting mid-page, or in the final clause. Every page is 95-112 words and holds exactly one queryable fact.
_about.why_controls: The single-topic pages are the load-bearing part. A mixed-topic page that ranks badly proves nothing on its own, because topic count and fact depth both moved. If a single-topic page ALSO loses rank when its fact is in the final clause, the cause is depth or length and heterogeneity is a red herring.
_about.built_blind: Written before any fix existed and without knowing what fix might apply, so it cannot be tuned toward a conclusion. Realistic rather than adversarial: real annual reports do put six subjects in an executive summary, and small teams really do write a combined 'Grounds and Security' page.
_about.scored_separately: Its own block so it cannot move the 33-case single-document headline, which is quoted across sessions.
_about.competitors: Pages 10-12 are topically dedicated to a probe question and do NOT hold its answer. Added after the first nine all ranked first, because that probe was missing the variable md-10 has: there the answer page competes with a page entirely about the question's subject. dp-10/11/12 hold depth at 'lead' and vary only the answer page's topic count, so any rank loss is attributable.
